name: Gfx_Pica_WriteTextureStatePacket
signature: u32* Gfx_Pica_WriteTextureStatePacket(u8* enable, u32* cmdBuf, int append, int extended)
summary: Appends a PICA200 texture-environment command packet to cmdBuf: command 0x00E40103 (TEXTURE_ENV config) plus register writes 0x008B and 0x0130, converting the float colour/scale fields of the state record to fixed point and masking with the 'enable' byte. Emitted during scene setup from Event_ClearActorSlots.
evidence: Body writes PICA command words 0x00E40103/0x000F008B/0x000F0130 and packs floats with VectorFloatToUnsigned, i.e. a texture-unit state packet; register 0x0130 is TEXUNIT0_BORDER_COLOR and 0x0103 the TEXENV config, so the 'texture state' wording is supported even though the single caller (Event_ClearActorSlots) is a field routine.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_InitFromHandle
summary: Looks up a player object with func_00556C48(handle+8) and resets its playback fields (+0x18/+0x1C/+0x20 to 0, +0x24 to 0.5f, +0x28 to 1, +0x29 to 0). The whole body sits behind a condition flag Ghidra could not recover (in_ZR), so both the guard and the owner class remain unverified.
evidence: Still damaged decompilation: the in_ZR guard decides whether the initialisation happens at all, and the lookup helper 0x00556C48 is unnamed, so neither 'sequence player' nor 'from handle' can be confirmed. Callee 0x00556BA4 sits in the sound work-buffer block, which only supports the Sound_ subsystem.

name: maybe_Actor_IsHandleFree
summary: Predicate: returns 1 when the reference word at actor+4 is null or the slot test 0x00643744 reports the slot unused, i.e. it reports that this actor handle slot is free. Only caller is SpiritMessage.
evidence: No new context: the single caller (SpiritMessage) uses the result as a yes/no gate, and the callee is itself still a maybe_. The null-reference shape fits 'slot free' rather than 'actor alive', but the actor record type is not proven.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_IsVisibleOrForced
summary: Three-way gate returning true when the index at +0x28 is non-negative, or the object at +0x24 is set and its active probe (0x00649BFC) says so, or the force byte at +0x2C is set. Nine Field_Object_GetKindNRecord accessors call it before returning a kind record, so it is a record-availability gate rather than a UI part visibility flag.
evidence: New caller evidence contradicts the 'Ui_Part' attribution: all named callers are Field_Object_GetKind0/1/2/4/6/7/9/10Record, so this is a field-object record gate. The three inputs are still only described structurally, so the exact meaning (visible / forced / present) is not settled and the name is left as maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_NotifyChild
summary: Two-step virtual forwarder: calls self->vtbl[+0x70](self) and then invokes slot +0x08 on the object it returned. Reads as 'ask this object for its related object and notify it', but neither direction nor the slot meanings are established.
evidence: No callers and no vtable placement, so nothing new supports either 'notify' or 'child'; both slots (+0x70 producer, +0x08 consumer) are unnamed. Kept as maybe_ with the direction uncertainty stated.

name: maybe_Actor_IsHandleSlotUnused
summary: Slot-unused test: returns 1 only when the sub-object test 0x0062F680(&actor->f_1F38) succeeds, the reference at +0x144 is null and bit 0 of +0x148 is clear. Used only by the sibling handle predicate 0x00640EC4.
evidence: No new named context: the only caller is still the maybe_ predicate at 0x00640EC4 and the probe 0x0062F680 is unnamed (the call-graph edge to 0x0062F5C8 does not match the body), so 'handle slot' remains inferred from the three null/flag tests.

name: maybe_Field_FindObjectInListA
signature: u32 maybe_Field_FindObjectInListA(void* self, u32* out, int slot, u32 key, u8 mask)
summary: Walks the intrusive list at self+0x18 and returns the first entry whose +0xF8 flag byte intersects mask and whose per-slot key at entry+slot*0xC+0x20 matches key; on success it writes the match value and the owner bytes self+0x21/self+0x22 into out.
evidence: No callers and the key comparator 0x0062AA7C is unnamed, so the list owner and the out[] layout still cannot be pinned; only the list-walk shape is certain. Callee 0x0062AA08 Object_IsHandleAlive does not appear in the body, so even that edge is unreliable.

name: maybe_Field_FindObjectInListB
signature: u32 maybe_Field_FindObjectInListB(void* self, u8* out, u32 key, u8 mask)
summary: Variant of 0x00643FE4 over the same intrusive list: matches the entry's own field at +0x10 instead of a per-slot key and writes the entry type byte (+0x1C) plus the owner bytes into out.
evidence: Still no caller and no named comparator, so the owner of the list is unknown; the only solid fact is that it is a near-copy of 0x00643FE4 with the key taken from entry+0x10.

name: maybe_Object_IsNestedCounterBehind
summary: 32-byte thunk: calls 0x00669DD4 on the pointer stored at object+0x2C (Ghidra's maybe_scaleValue) and returns whether it is non-zero. The callee is a mid-entry inside the MoLive movie-audio blob, so the real comparison is not visible here.
evidence: No new context; the callee 0x00669DD4 is an interior address of the MoLive_Stream block (its named neighbour is MoLive_Stream_BindPacket 0x006698AC), so 'counter comparison' cannot be verified and even the owning subsystem is unclear.

name: Data_LookupIndexById
summary: Lazily builds the 0x10-byte-entry data-manager container (0xA24 bytes, vtable g_gameDataManagerVtable), looks the row up with 0x0063E3C8 and returns its byte at +0x10, or 0xFF when the id is unknown. Ghidra typed the id as a u8 pointer, but the body reads *id, so it is a by-value byte id.
evidence: The body is a complete 'get index byte for id, 0xFF = not found' lookup: container construction, 0x0063E3C8(dataManager,*id) and 'return record->f_10 else 0xFF'. Two named UI callers (Ui_Window_AttachChildToFreeSlot, Ui_Marker_RetryBindTarget_Label) use it as a table lookup; only the record type behind 0x0063E3C8 remains unnamed, which is why this stays at 0.5.

name: PartyMember_GetSpellRecordFlag
summary: Calls virtual slot +0x64 with index 0; when that sub-object's byte +0x10 is zero, returns bit 0 of the flag word at +0x208 of the record pointed to by self+0x1260. self+0x1260 lies inside the 0x12EC-byte PartyMember record, and +0x208 is the documented SpellRecord u16 flag word.
evidence: FACTS.md pins SpellRecord flags at +0x208 and PartyMember size to 0x12EC, so the +0x1260 pointer field can only be a per-member sub-record (spell table) and the tail read is a SpellRecord flag bit. Still no caller, hence 0.5 rather than higher.

name: maybe_Ui_GetScaledTime
summary: Entry of a 1272-byte merged blob of small accessors; the only visible fragment calls 0x0065D3B8 for a tick value and converts it to float with VectorUnsignedToFloat using the FPSCR rounding mode. The 19 callers belong to the interior accessors, not to this address.
evidence: Confirms the blob diagnosis: caller names are all UI panels/list/message windows and the only callee is 0x0065D1E0 in the Gfx mesh block, so this address is a merged entry point rather than a UI time helper. Nothing identifies which interior accessor the tick conversion belongs to.

name: maybe_Field_GetSceneState
summary: Returns 3 when the global probe 0x006281C8 reports ready and 0 otherwise. The same probe is used by 0x00654F34 as a player/interaction readiness gate, so this is best described as 'scene state 3 or 0' rather than a general state getter.
evidence: The probe 0x006281C8 is shared with 0x00654F34 (where it gates grid interaction), which weakens 'scene state' and suggests a readiness/phase enum. Only caller is Field_FindObjectByMode; the rest of the 0xBC-byte body is lost, so the enum values cannot be mapped.

name: maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_IsRecipeRow
summary: Row predicate: returns 0 when the sub-object at row+0x14 reports state 1 with a valid index (+0xC0) whose 8-byte record id is not the 0x306 sentinel, and otherwise returns the result of the row's virtual +0x54 ready test.
evidence: The address is a slot in the UI widget table 0x007808E0 next to Ui_Widget_* entries, which supports 'UI row predicate' but no caller or string connects it to the smith menu; 0x306 is the field-trigger count from FACTS, not proven as the sentinel here.

name: maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_AllSlotsIdle
summary: Idle predicate: calls a virtual test on row+0x2BC, then requires every element of the row+0x278..0x280 pair to be idle, the registered handle at row+0x284 to be valid in the global handle table, and the row's virtual +0x54 ready test to pass.
evidence: No caller; vtable neighbours are Ui_DrawList_InsertWindowNodes and Ui_Screen_IsAnyChildBusy, so this is a generic widget idle/handle-validity predicate. Nothing ties it to a smith menu.

name: maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_IsMaterialValid
summary: Mirror of 0x0064D824 through row+0x274: returns 0 when that sub-object reports state 1 with a valid index (+0xAC) whose 8-byte record id is not the 0x306 sentinel, and 1 otherwise.
evidence: The only caller is the unnamed-by-subsystem maybe_Field_Object2D_AdvanceTouchTransition, so the smith-menu / material reading is unsupported; the body is still the same 'state 1 + valid index + non-sentinel id' test, which is all the name asserts.

name: maybe_Actor_IsHandleFreeD
summary: Template copy of the handle test at 0x00643744 anchored on actor+0x34 -> +0x1E18: returns 1 when the owner/reference chain is null and the actor's reference at +4 is null with bit 0 of +8 clear. Despite the old 'Alive' wording it reports a FREE slot, exactly like 0x00640EC4/0x00643744.
evidence: New reading of the body: the final two conjuncts are both null tests (actor+4 == 0 and (actor+8 & 1) == 0), so the function can only be true for an unused slot - the previous 'IsHandleAliveD' name stated the opposite. 15 callers, mostly Ui_EquipmentWindow_* and Ui_MessageVoice_*, all use it as an 'is this slot empty' gate.

name: Ui_List_GetScrollRowIndex
summary: Turns the list's scroll state into an absolute row index: base = u16 at list[0xE]+0xC, offset = virtual +0x68, index = base + row*5 - offset, then resolves it through 0x00650860/0x00648348; returns 0xFFFFFFFF when the row array at list[0x15] is null.
evidence: Six named list-window callers (Ui_DiveWindow, Ui_RecordWindow_Update/HandleInput, Ui_RecordDetailWindow, Ui_ListWidget_GetCursorValue, Ui_JackpotScreen) all need the same 'which absolute row is under the cursor' value; the 5-word row stride and the +0x68 first-visible-row virtual match the list-window layout. The two callees carry clearly wrong names (Item_ConsumeForCraft, Party_GetSlotCountPlusPending), so the name stays at 0.5.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_QueryStatusPair
signature: void maybe_Battle_Unit_QueryStatusPair(void* actor, void* unit, u8* outFlagA, u8* outFlagB)
summary: Fills two status flags for a unit: (0,0) when any of the unit's +0x54 bytes is set or the actor's virtual +0x50 reports busy, otherwise maps monster state 6 to (1,0), 7 to (0,1) and 0xC to (0,0).
evidence: Still no callers, so the two output bytes are never observed consumed; the state mapping depends on 0x00669250 returning 6/7/0xC, and that helper is unnamed. The call-graph callees (Field_NpcCheckSight, Actor_ResolveReferenceObject) do not appear in the body.

name: Field_QueryFourBoxes
signature: void Field_QueryFourBoxes(void* owner, int scene, int layer, int* rect, int* grow, int* grow2, u8* results)
summary: Runs the owner's scene query callback (owner+0x48) four times, each time with the base rectangle grown by the next pair from grow2, and stores the four boolean results into results[0..3]. Used by the area-overlap and grid-move tests to probe four offset boxes.
evidence: Two confident named callers, Field_TestAreaOverlapA and Field_TestAreaOverlapB, both pass rectangles and consume four booleans, and the body is exactly a 4-iteration loop over the owner+0x48 query callback with growing extents. The third caller is still a maybe_, but the two confident ones settle the role.

name: Ui_ListWindow_GetRowFlag
summary: Returns the flag byte of the row under the cursor: index = (base u16 at listWindow[0xE]+0xC) + cursor*10 - firstVisibleRow(vtable+0x68), read from the 10-byte row array at listWindow+0x78.
evidence: Five confident callers across two unrelated systems (Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdateCounter/Confirm and Ui_CasinoSlot*_Init) all use it as a per-row flag getter, and the 10-byte row stride matches the list-window layout used by 0x0064E88C. The callers only prove 'row flag of the selected row', not what the flag means.

name: maybe_Pack_WriteWordQuadAt60
summary: Serialises the four u32 words at record+0x60..0x6C through writer->vtbl[+0x10](writer, index, &word).
evidence: No caller, no rodata reference and no vtable neighbour, so neither the record class nor the writer class can be named; only the loop shape is verified.

name: maybe_Pack_WriteWordQuadAt50
summary: Twin of 0x00654DA4 writing the four words at record+0x50..0x5C through the same writer virtual; same unknown record/writer classes.
evidence: Identical body to 0x00654DA4 except the base offset (0x50); still no caller or table reference to identify the types.

name: maybe_Field_TryPlayerInteractGated
summary: Returns the AND of the global readiness probe 0x006281C8 and the grid-interaction query 0x0065172C for the request. The only caller is the still-unnamed maybe_Battle_CanUseItemOnSelf.
evidence: The probe 0x006281C8 is the same readiness gate used by 0x0064C82C, so 'player ready' is plausible, but the sole caller is itself a maybe_ and the grid query 0x0065172C is a maybe_ too; no independent evidence for the 'try interact' wording.

name: maybe_Effect_ActorTrail_LiteralPool
summary: Not a function: literal-pool data following the effect code, misdecoded as Thumb; the decompiled body is halt_baddata() and the only xref comes from the neighbouring Effect_ActorTrail_ShouldFinishB.

name: maybe_Pack_ReadInline6A
signature: bool maybe_Pack_ReadInline6A(void* dst, u32 arg2, u32* outSize, u32 avail)
summary: Interior switch case of an inline-record reader: copies six bytes from the record pointer carried in r12+4 to dst when avail >= 6 and reports size 6.
evidence: Still damaged (in_r12 holds the record pointer) and no callers, which is expected for an interior case entry; nothing identifies the container format, so only 'copy 6 bytes' is verified.

name: maybe_Pack_ReadLengthPrefixedRecord
signature: bool maybe_Pack_ReadLengthPrefixedRecord(void* record, void* dst, u32* outSize, u32* avail)
summary: Copies a five-byte inline header from record+5 and then the payload at record+0xC of length u16 at record+8, reporting 5+length; refuses when fewer than that many bytes remain.
evidence: Body is intact and the 5 + u16-at-+8 layout is clear (func_0011FFC4 copies the header, func_00116A14 = __aeabi_memcpy copies the payload), but there are still no callers and the record class is unknown.

name: maybe_Pack_ReadInline6B
signature: bool maybe_Pack_ReadInline6B(void* dst, u32 arg2, u32* outSize, u32 avail)
summary: Second six-byte inline reader, byte-identical to 0x006583E8; same damaged in_r12 shape and same 6-byte copy when avail >= 6.
evidence: Confirmed as a duplicate of 0x006583E8 with no callers; the container/record class is still unknown.

name: maybe_Pack_ReadInline3
signature: bool maybe_Pack_ReadInline3(void* dst, u32 arg2, u32* outSize, u32 avail)
summary: Three-byte inline reader copying from r12+4 to dst and reporting 3 when avail >= 3; same damaged shape as the six-byte variants.
evidence: Only the copy length differs from 0x006583E8/0x00658480; no callers, record class unknown.

name: maybe_Svc_Cecd_Command12
signature: u32 maybe_Svc_Cecd_Command12(void* session, void* buffer, u32 size)
summary: Zeroes a 0x60-byte buffer and issues CECD command 0x12 (buffer, 0x60, outSize, size, 2, 0x12) through the session virtual at +0x34; maps a successfully-written result to 0xC8810BEF when nothing was written.
evidence: The command number, the 0x60 buffer and the 0xC8810BEF CECD result code are all visible and consistent, but there is no CECD command table in the project to say what command 0x12 means and no callers, so the specific operation cannot be named.

name: maybe_Svc_Blob_SerializeTail
signature: bool maybe_Svc_Blob_SerializeTail(u32 arg1, u32 value, u32* other, u32 src)
summary: Damaged tail of the archive path resolver: when the caller's Z flag is clear it compares 8 bytes (func_001009DC) and returns 1 on equality, else 0. Called only from Fs_Archive_ResolvePath, so it is an 8-byte key comparison rather than a serialiser.
evidence: The body is an 8-byte comparison whose result is folded into 'return arg1', and the only caller is Fs_Archive_ResolvePath - the old 'Serialize' wording is unsupported, but the in_ZR dependence means this is a split tail, not a standalone function, so the name is kept as maybe_.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetPointerValueA
summary: Resolves the +0x34 relative-offset sub-table of the sequence data via 0x0065FB98 and returns its first word.
evidence: The three siblings resolve three distinct relative offsets of the same sequence record (+0x34 here, +0x2C at 0x00660CAC, +0x1C at 0x00660E0C) through the Sound_SeqResource resolver, so the family is a set of typed field getters; the exact meaning of the returned word is still unknown, hence 0.5.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqField_NotifyChange
summary: Resolves the sequence sub-object via func_0065F678 and, when it is non-null, calls the tag-to-kind mapping 0x0065FF20 and discards the result. No store and no callee side effect are visible, so 'NotifyChange' is unsupported.
evidence: Confirmed no observable effect: the only callee is the pure tag mapping 0x0065FF20 and its result is dropped, so whatever the original did was lost in decompilation (Ghidra trap: dropped result). No caller exists to show intent.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetPointerValueB
summary: Resolves the +0x2C relative-offset sub-table of the sequence data via 0x0065FBB0 and returns its first word; sibling of the +0x34 and +0x1C getters.
evidence: Resolver 0x0065FBB0 is 'ldr r1,[r0,#0x2c]; add r0,r0,r1', so this variant is verifiably the +0x2C field getter of the same record family as 0x00660A80/0x00660E0C. Word meaning still unknown.

name: Sound_SeqField_GetPointerValueC
summary: Resolves the +0x1C relative-offset sub-table of the sequence data via 0x0065FBC8 and returns its first word; third member of the pointer-getter family.
evidence: Resolver 0x0065FBC8 adds *(u32*)(self+0x1C), distinct from the +0x34/+0x2C variants, and the body returns the resolved table's first word. Callers are absent so the word's meaning is unverified.

name: maybe_Sound_Seq_ExecuteChannelCommand_Tail
summary: Damaged mid-function split symbol: the ARM switch tail of Sound_Seq_ExecuteChannelCommand misdisassembled as Thumb, producing halt_baddata and unaff_/in_ZR/coprocessor_ operands; not a real entry point.
evidence: Confirmed split tail: body is unaff_/coprocessor noise immediately after 0x00661974, and the 'caller' Ui_TrainingMessage_ReleaseTables is an xref artefact. Callees are Sound_SeqChannel_* helpers, so the enclosing function is the channel-command executor.

name: maybe_Sound_Curve_Evaluate
summary: Curve/envelope step evaluator: when the current step (+0x10) has reached the limit (+8), dispatches through the type table g_animTimelineTypeDispatchTable indexed by the type byte, with a special case for type 4 that caches the phase, and returns the count converted to float.
evidence: All three callers are sound code (Sound_Cwav_Open, Sound_WaveInfo_ParseFormat, Sound_Seq_ReadVarLenArg) and the dispatch table is a waveform/curve-type table with per-type callbacks and a phase for type 4, so 'Anim_Timeline' was the wrong subsystem; the exact curve semantic (envelope, LFO, waveform) is not identifiable, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Text_BuildCharTransform_Tail
summary: Damaged continuation fragment directly after Text_BuildCharTransform (0x00663FB8): stores character-transform quad words from unaff_ registers and in_s0..s3, then returns arg1+3. Not a separate function.
evidence: Confirmed continuation: 0x00663FB8 ends exactly at this address and the body only writes unaff_r4/r5/r7 and the incoming s registers; no callers.

name: Field_Object2D_PushTrailSample
signature: void Field_Object2D_PushTrailSample(void* object, void* unit, void* history)
summary: Shifts the three 12-byte position/state entries of the history buffer down by one and writes a new sample derived from unit+0x4C8, then refreshes the sprite chip range through Field2D_SpriteBlock_UpdateChipRange and Field_Object2D_CalcScreenRectA.
evidence: Body is a literal 3-entry ring shift (12-byte stride) followed by a sample push and the two named field-2D sprite helpers Field2D_SpriteBlock_UpdateChipRange and Field_Object2D_CalcScreenRectA, which is exactly a movement-history push for the 2D field object. No caller, so 'trail' vs 'path history' stays loose.

name: Field_Object2D_CalcScreenRectB
summary: Fills a 4-int screen rectangle from the sub-object at object+4 (position +0x78/+0x7C) with a constant 2x2 extent, transformed by func_0031A658; variant B of the 2D field-object rect family.
evidence: Same shape as the confirmed-sized family members 0x00668840/0x0066D9FC/0x0066DA64 (position from (object+4)->+0x78/+0x7C, extent then offset through 0x0031A658), so the variant letter is a disambiguator for identical-purpose copies; no caller pins which object kind uses variant B.

name: maybe_Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep_Tail
summary: Damaged continuation tail of 0x00667EA4 (Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep): a switch-branch that stores through unaff_r4 and was split off as a separate Thumb function.
evidence: 0x00667EA4 has size 0xEA and ends exactly here, and this fragment's only caller is 0x00667EA4; body stores unaff_r4/arg2/arg4, so it is not a standalone function.

name: Field_Object2D_GetAnimField16
summary: One-line getter for the u8 at +0x16 of the anim sub-object at (self+8)->+0x2B4; used by the map-chip layer packer to pick the chip variant.
evidence: Body is exactly 'return *(u8*)(*(int*)(*(int*)(self+8)+0x2B4)+0x16)' and the named caller Field2D_MapChip_PackLayerChipIds consumes it as a per-object anim field, so the accessor identity is certain; only the field's game meaning is unknown.

name: Field_Object2D_GetAnimField10
summary: One-line getter for the u16 at +0x10 of the anim sub-object at (self+8)->+0x2B4; read by the sprite node draw dispatch.
evidence: Body is a single u16 load at anim+0x10 and the named caller Field2D_SpriteNode_DispatchDraw uses it while building the draw call, consistent with a frame/palette index; the field's exact meaning is not established.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_StubFragmentA
summary: Interior fragment of an ARM accessor block misidentified as a 4-byte Thumb function; body contains byte-swap arithmetic on unaff_ registers and is not a real entry point.
evidence: Confirmed non-entry: 4-byte body, unaff_r6/r7 and stack-slot arithmetic that cannot belong to a function; no callers.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_StubFragmentB
summary: Second interior fragment of the same accessor block, 4 bytes, damaged byte-swap body with unaff_ registers; not a real function entry.

summary: Second interior fragment of the same accessor stub, identical damaged body to fragment D (in_OV, unaff_ registers); not a real entry point.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_StubFragmentF
summary: Third interior fragment of the accessor stub, same damaged four-word store body as D/E but writing through self itself; not a real function entry.
evidence: Same body pattern as fragments D/E; no callers.

name: Field_Object2D_CalcScreenRectD
summary: Computes the screen rectangle of a 2D field object from the sub-object at object+4: position +0x78/+0x7C, extents from the shorts at (sub+0x298)->+4/+6, then offset/extent through func_0031A658.

name: maybe_MoLive_Stream_ReadPcm_Tail
summary: Damaged continuation fragment of the movie-audio PCM read routine; the decompiled body is only halt_baddata(), so nothing about it can be verified.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_OnEvent_Subclass
summary: Event dispatch chain: offers the event to the object at self+0x24 (its virtual +8), then to Sound_SeqParam_NotifyChange's router 0x00660414, and finally to the class virtual +0x10 of self-0xC. Whoever returns non-zero stops the chain.
evidence: The callee Sound_SeqParam_NotifyChange anchors the class in the sound-sequence parameter block, and the two-stage 'handled?' chain is clear, but there are no callers and the self-0xC adjustment means this is a secondary-base entry, so 'OnEvent' stays a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorDelete_76AD28
summary: Releases the object at vtable 0x0076AD28 by calling Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub on its list node with delete flag 1. Treated as a deleting destructor, but no vtable-resident placement proves it.
evidence: The body is a single call to func_0029126C(&self->listNodePrev, 1) which the doc identifies as Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub; that fits a destructor body, but with no callers and no vtable slot proof the class and the 'Delete' part remain unverified.

name: Field_Object_BindModelTransform
summary: Resets the transform of the embedded node (self-0x1330) via func_003CDF74, points its model slot at that node, and when a field actor is present copies the actor model position (+0x9C/+0xA0/+0xA4) into the object transform and clears model+0x72C.
evidence: Body is a complete bind step: reset transform, install node pointer at self-0x1380+0x2294, then copy the three model position words obtained through func_005F5818(actor->f_110) and clear a model flag. Callee names (Gfx_EffectPart_ResetToDefault, 0x001F4CF8 transform copy) support the reading, though no caller proves which object kind binds.

name: Field_Object2D_CalcScreenRectE
summary: Fills a 4-int screen rectangle from the sub-object at object+4 (position +0x78/+0x7C) with a constant 2x2 extent via func_0031A658; variant E of the 2D field-object rect family.
evidence: Identical body to 0x00667D78 (same 2x2 constant extent and +0x78/+0x7C position), which is itself part of the confirmed CalcScreenRect family; the letter only disambiguates copies.
